web_title: 9. Both Sides of the Aisle, Likely Outcomes & REJECTED Action Plan
book_title: Chapter 9: Bull vs. Bear Steelman, Expected Value & Why We Reject New Capital at $286.20
question: Weighing both sides honestly, why do our DCF and asymmetry gates downgrade ABBV to REJECTED (TIER_0) with 100% cash preservation?

epigraph.quote: The discipline to pass on a good company at a fair price is what keeps capital intact for great asymmetries.
epigraph.author: Institutional Risk & Capital Allocation Discipline

web_blocks.title: Two-Sided Steelman: The Strongest Bull Case vs. The Strongest Bear Case

web_blocks.html: The Bull Steelman: AbbVie replaced a $21 billion peak blockbuster without shrinking earnings. Skyrizi ($21.8B FY26E) and Rinvoq ($10.3B FY26E) are scaling past $32 billion combined, with Rinvoq's U.S. exclusivity protected until April 2037 [3, 18]. Neuroscience ($13.0B FY26E) adds a second double-digit engine, while the October 29, 2026 D.C. District Court ruling vacating CMS's Round 3 IRA selection of Botox removes a major 2028 overhang [3]. Coupled with a 2.54% dividend yield (+5.2% hike to $1.82/quarter), bulls see steady compounding toward $365.00.

The Bear Steelman: At $286.20, the market already prices in 7.8% 10-year FCF compounding while ignoring heavy claims ahead of equity. Q3 2026 gross debt sits at $80.90 billion ($70.13B net debt) with a -$4.58 billion stockholders' deficit, $27.31 billion in contingent consideration liabilities ($2,796M paid in 9M 2026, +28.0% YoY), and ~$4.09B–$5.02B annual acquired IPR&D [3, 21]. Up to 43% single-wholesaler U.S. concentration, 2027 IRA cuts on Vraylar and Linzess, Aesthetics softness, and serial M&A delay 2.0x deleveraging past 2028 [1, 3, 18]. Under our 10-year DCF ($21.50B FCF, 8.5% WACC, 2.5% g, -$81.25B net debt + Skyrizi claim), Base fair value is $315.00 and Bear downside is $235.00 (-17.9%).

web_blocks.takeaway: Across all three horizons, ABBV is downgraded from ACCUMULATE_ON_DIP (TIER_2) to REJECTED (TIER_0, VALUATION) with 100% marginal cash preserved.

web_blocks.title: Actionable Re-Entry Triggers & Downtrend Cash Discipline

web_blocks.html: Re-Underwriting Trigger (When REJECTED Could Flip): Do not allocate new equity or options capital to ABBV at $286.20 or at the $278.20 shelf. Re-underwrite only if (1) ABBV pulls back toward ~$255–$262 where Base R:R against a re-anchored stop clears 2.0:1, OR (2) debt paydown + Q1 2027 guidance lift 10Y DCF Base fair value above $330 while S&P 500 breadth recovers above 50% and US portfolio cash rebuilds toward the 22.0% Downtrend floor.

book_paragraphs: Great investing requires knowing when a strong business is simply priced too close to fair value to justify risking scarce cash. In Round 1, we leaned on multiple expansion to 18.5x forward earnings and an assumed pause in M&A to justify a $340.00 target and an Accumulate on Dip verdict. When we strip out that optimism and value AbbVie strictly on a 10-year Discounted Cash Flow model—deducting $81.25 billion for net debt and Skyrizi contingent consideration claims—the picture changes.

Base fair value drops to $315.00 per share, and probability-weighted Expected Value drops to $305.00 (25% Bear at $235.00, 55% Base at $315.00, 20% Bull at $365.00). Even if we wait patiently for a pullback to $278.20 support with a $252.23 stop, the Base reward-to-risk ratio is only 1.42:1 and the Expected Value ratio is 1.03:1. Both fail our 1.50:1 minimum hurdle. Combined with a 10-distribution-day S&P 500 Downtrend (38.8% above the 50-day average) and only 3.38% US portfolio cash ($2,540.35 of $75,110.60 NAV) against a 22.0% cash floor, we reject new capital allocation (TIER_0, VALUATION) and keep 100% in cash.

book_subsections.title: Why We Also Decline the $290/$340 Bull Call Debit Spread
paragraphs: The automated options scan flagged a February 19, 2027 $290/$340 bull call debit spread at $13.23 per share ($1,323.00 per contract). We explicitly decline that trade (NO_OPTIONS_EDGE). First, the short $340 call sits well above our $315.00 DCF Base fair value and $305.00 Expected Value. Second, $1,323.00 represents 176.1 basis points of our $75,110.60 portfolio NAV and consumes 52.1% of our entire $2,540.35 US cash balance in a Downtrend regime. Standing aside protects both cash and risk budget.

Finally, we monitor three objective signposts each quarter before revisiting this REJECTED rating: (1) quarterly contingent consideration cash payouts and net debt trajectory toward the 2.0x EBITDA target, (2) Skyrizi and Rinvoq net revenue growth relative to the >$32 billion FY2026 run-rate, and (3) appellate outcomes on the October 29, 2026 Botox IRA District Court injunction alongside 2027 Vraylar and Linzess net pricing.

book_subsections.title: Stress-Testing Both Sides: What Would Make Us Change Our Mind?
paragraphs: Rejecting a stock today does not mean ignoring AbbVie forever. Our verdict reflects price, balance-sheet claims, and market regime as of November 20, 2026, not a permanent judgment on the company's science. If AbbVie pulls back into the $255 to $262 range during a broader market sell-off while fundamentals hold steady, the reward-to-risk math against a re-anchored structural stop would easily clear 2.0:1. At that lower price, the 2.54% dividend yield would rise toward 2.8%, and the market would no longer demand 7.8% ten-year FCF compounding.

Alternatively, our Base-Case intrinsic value could move higher without a stock pullback if management demonstrates two concrete shifts in early 2027. First, AbbVie would need to pause major debt-funded acquisitions and apply residual free cash flow directly toward retiring the $80.90 billion debt load, pulling net debt down meaningfully from $70.13 billion. Second, formal FY2027 guidance in February 2027 would need to show that Skyrizi, Rinvoq, and Neuroscience easily absorb the statutory Medicare IRA cuts on Vraylar and Linzess while the October 2026 Botox IRA injunction survives government appeal.

book_subsections.title: Capital Preservation Plan: 100% Cash and Zero Options Allocation
paragraphs: Because ABBV is not currently held in any Schwab, Robinhood, or options account (0 shares, NOT_HELD), executing this downgrade requires zero forced selling. Our redeployment plan keeps 100% of marginal capital in cash (HOLD_CASH_FOR_PULLBACK). While healthcare peers such as McKesson (MCK) remain on our active shortlist and Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) serves as a balance-sheet benchmark, both stay at 0% allocation while US portfolio cash sits at 3.38% against a 22.0% Downtrend floor.

Standing aside on both ABBV common stock and the $1,323 February 2027 $290/$340 call spread preserves over half of our remaining US cash buffer. In a 10-distribution-day Downtrend, protecting liquidity until breadth recovers above 50% and true 2:1+ asymmetries appear is the highest-return decision available.

book_subsections.title: Comparing the Three Horizons: Short-Term, Medium-Term, and Long-Term
paragraphs: Across all three investment horizons, discipline points to the same conclusion. Over the short term (1 to 3 months), a 10-distribution-day S&P 500 Downtrend (38.8% above 50-DMA) and 3.38% US portfolio cash against a 22.0% floor argue against chasing a 0.85:1 CMP reward-to-risk setup. Over the medium term (6 to 18 months), our $315.00 Base fair value and $305.00 Expected Value fail the 1.50:1 hurdle even from the $278.20 support shelf (1.42:1 Base and 1.03:1 EV).

Over the long term (3 to 5 years), AbbVie remains a high-quality Compounder Pass business backed by Skyrizi, Rinvoq's 2037 U.S. exclusivity, and a growing Neuroscience franchise. Yet long-term business quality does not override entry price. Assigning REJECTED (TIER_0, VALUATION) today keeps our dry powder intact until either price drops into the $255–$262 zone or deleveraging lifts intrinsic value meaningfully above $330.

To make our pass decision completely transparent, we also document the exact parameters of the declined options setup in Section 13. The February 19, 2027 $290/$340 bull call debit spread carried a $13.23 net debit ($1,323.00 per contract), equal to 176.1 basis points of our $75,110.60 consolidated NAV and 52.1% of our $2,540.35 US cash balance. Accepting a capped-upside call spread whose upper strike ($340) sits $25 above our $315 Base DCF value—while consuming over half of remaining US cash in a Downtrend—violates both valuation and position-sizing discipline.

As our final underwriting rule, we refuse to stretch valuation multiples or ignore balance-sheet claims simply to keep a Compounder Pass name on the buy list. AbbVie's science and commercial execution are real, yet at $286.20 the stock prices in smooth sailing while carrying $80.90 billion of gross debt and $27.31 billion of contingent consideration liabilities. Passing today protects capital for cleaner setups.

book_callouts.title: CHAPTER 9 VERDICT: REJECTED (TIER_0, VALUATION) — 100% CASH
book_callouts.text: ABBV is NOT_HELD (0 shares). New capital is REJECTED on valuation (1.42:1 Base R:R / 1.03:1 EV R:R at $278.20 support vs. $252.23 stop), and the $1,323 2027-02-19 $290/$340 call spread is DECLINED (52.1% of US cash). Keep 100% in cash.
